clue.text: Be economical if you want extra money

definitions.meaning: to save money is to hold back funds rather than spend them
surplus funds left over for treats

explanation.surface: Advice to a saver: cut back if you want something left over to spend.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a verb phrase it means saving funds; read as a noun it is surplus funds kept in reserve.

clue.text: Look which makes Peter lose heart

indicators.note: the heart of a five-letter name is its central letter, which is dropped here

explanation.surface: Someone is told what Peter would look like without his middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose heart' removes the middle letter T of PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look closely, squinting at something.

clue.text: Dealer's'clique allowed to acquire a decorative hair-piece

parts.note: a ring is a group of dealers colluding at auction
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A cartel of traders is permitted to buy some ornamental hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A RING is a group of dealers who agree not to bid against each other at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl of hair hanging in a spiral is an ornament worn on the head.

clue.text: Unable to rest in peace because of a witch's spell

parts.note: can't means unable
RIP is the abbreviation of rest in peace on gravestones

explanation.surface: A soul cannot lie quietly in the grave because a witch has cursed it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a magic incantation or charm, the kind a witch casts.

clue.text: He looks and looks ahead

parts.note: describes someone who both sees and foresees the future, a prophet

explanation.definitionFit: A prophet is one who sees, and one who sees into what is coming.

clue.text: The team mates I settled together

indicators.note: settled means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports player says the squad settled down as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Simultaneously, at once, all together in one moment.

clue.text: Normal lines of transmission for BBC1 and ITV?

definitions.text: Normal lines of transmission for BBC1 and ITV?

parts.words: Normal lines of transmission for BBC1 and ITV?
parts.note: BBC1 and ITV are the standard British TV stations, and the phrase also means the proper official routes of communication

explanation.walkthrough: BBC1 and ITV are long-standing mainstream British television channels.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the regular official routes for communication, and literally the standard TV stations.

clue.text: Ten Eton nurses abused? Fiddlesticks!

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or knocked about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An outraged cry about a school's nurses being badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation dismissing something as rubbish, like 'balderdash!'

clue.text: A sailing ship heading South needs a chart, but only a rough one

indicators.note: heading here means going at the front of the vessel's name, so the compass point goes first

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel
a map is a chart

explanation.surface: A navigator needs a chart to sail south, but makes do with a crude one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' puts S in front of KETCH; 'one' in the definition stands for a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A quickly drawn plan of an area is a crude chart.

clue.text: Difficult man has skill, yet lacks finer feelings

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun: someone with this lacks compassion

parts.note: hard means difficult
he is a male pronoun, so a man
art means skill

explanation.surface: A tough fellow is talented but has no sensitivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Callousness or lack of compassion is a want of tender emotions.

clue.text: German Chancellor may get black eye with it in the East

definitions.text: may get black eye with it in the East
definitions.meaning: a dark powder used in Asia and the Middle East to darken the eyelids

explanation.surface: A German leader might end up with a shiner on a trip east.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl was the West German, then German, head of government; the cosmetic darkens the eyes.

clue.text: Show obvious disapproval of a large cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone frowns at a barman serving a big mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare angrily is to make one's displeasure plain.

clue.text: The baby's mother has a double degree

indicators.note: double means the piece is written twice

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A highly qualified woman with two degrees has just had a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's word for its female parent.

clue.text: A lot of politicians do

definitions.meaning: a celebration or social gathering, as in 'a big do'

explanation.definitionFit: A political organisation; also a festive gathering, which British English calls a do.

clue.text: The drinks taken by superior people, but not the teetotaller

indicators.note: but not means leave out the teetotaller from the superior people

parts.note: one's betters are people of higher rank
TT stands for teetotal, an abstainer

explanation.surface: Upper-class folk drink, except for the one who abstains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales and lagers are drinks.

clue.text: It once encouraged Anglicans to hold a rehearsal

definitions.meaning: a 17th-century English law requiring office-holders to be Church of England members
to try out a performance piece

explanation.walkthrough: The Test Acts required holders of public office in England to take Church of England communion.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1673 law barred non-Anglicans from public office; also, to try out a stage performance.

clue.text: Holey holy creed wholly revised

parts.note: pi is short for pious, holy

indicators.note: wholly revised means completely rewritten, so the letters of the statement of faith are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church's statement of faith is completely rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) comes from 'holy'; 'wholly revised' turns CREED into ERCED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pierced has holes punched through it.

clue.text: Pet found in many of Birmingham's terraces

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pet animal is common in the terraced houses of Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent kept in cages as a pet.

clue.text: One rooted in the Liberal tradition

definitions.meaning: in mathematics a root sign, and something relating to roots
the ... were the reforming wing of the British Liberals

explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin for root; a reformist Liberal was a Radical.

clue.text: Refuse to make period costume before time

indicators.note: before places the costume ahead of the time

parts.note: garb is clothing, a costume
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A designer has to create historical dress ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish or waste thrown out is refuse.

clue.text: Well done! Drink up, old chum

parts.note: good! is a word of praise

indicators.note: up in a down entry reverses the word

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Praising a friend and urging them to finish a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LAP to PAL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A close friend or mate.

clue.text: A section of the Bible become opposed to

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'A section of the Bible become opposed to' gives A + NT but no I; a word (probably 'I') seems lost in OCR and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: A section of the Bible become opposed to

clue.text: That fool Amin upset Transport Officer

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: TO is the abbreviation of Transport Officer

explanation.surface: A Ugandan dictator overturns an official's plans, proving himself a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person is a fool.

clue.text: Exceptional person, but deficient in writing and arithmetic?

definitions.text: Exceptional person, but deficient in writing and arithmetic?

parts.words: Exceptional person, but deficient in writing and arithmetic?
parts.note: a unique individual, and someone with only one of the three Rs (reading), lacking the other two

explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; lacking two leaves one R.
explanation.definitionFit: A unique, remarkable individual; also someone with just a single R of reading, writing and arithmetic.

clue.text: Advanced in fast time

definitions.meaning: the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.definitionFit: Loaned out; also the Christian season of fasting before Easter.

clue.text: Note played very loudly caused ill-temper

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
ff (fortissimo) is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A musician plays a note too loud and annoys everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty fit of annoyance or sulk.

clue.text: I am sensible, but you'd never notice

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
sensible in its old sense means able to be sensed

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be sensible yet says nobody would notice them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sensible' is used in its older meaning, perceivable by the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Too slight to be detected is unnoticeable.

clue.text: The genre of painting that is not yet dead

definitions.meaning: a category of art showing arranged inanimate objects
continuing to have breath and vitality

explanation.surface: A kind of picture-making that has not died out yet.
explanation.definitionFit: An art form depicting fruit, flowers and the like; read literally, a body that remains alive.
